caveats:
This product contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2019), processed by ESA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore.

These are preliminary maps derived from satellite radar and should be used as guidance only. Coloured pixels may include false positives, and their absence does not mean an absence of damage or flooding.
dataset_source: NASA JPL-Caltech ARIA team; Earth Observatory of Singapore
methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

# Philippines Earthquake: Damage Proxy Maps, Oct 2019

The Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) team at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and Caltech, in collaboration with the Earth Observatory of Singapore (EOS), produced these damage proxy maps for Philippines Earthquake (Oct 2019) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images. Each map is a separate ZIP below with its GeoTIFF, a KMZ for Google Earth, the PNG figures and a text file describing how it was made and how to read it.

## Maps in this dataset

- **Philippines - ARIA Damage Proxy Map v0.4** (superseded)
- **Philippines - ARIA Damage Proxy Map v0.4**

**More map details and files:** <https://sf.earthobservatory.sg/event/EOS_ARIA-SG_201910_Philipines_Earthquake>

**Copyright:** Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2019) processed by ESA, the ARIA team at NASA-JPL and Caltech, and EOS.

organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.

title: Philippines Earthquake: Damage Proxy Maps, Oct 2019

resources.description:
Philippines - ARIA Damage Proxy Map v0.4

ZIP containing: GeoTIFF, KMZ, PNG, TXT.

Superseded by a later version in this dataset.

The Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) team at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and California Institute of Technology (Caltech) in Pasadena, California, in collaboration with the Earth Observatory of Singapore (EOS), created this Damage Proxy Map (DPM) depicting areas in Philippines that are likely damaged (shown by red and yellow pixels) as a result of Earthquake Tuesday (October 29) local time. The map was derived from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data acquired around 5am (local time) on November 8, 2019 by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellites operated by the European Space Agency (ESA). The pre-event images were taken before (October 2, 2019 and October 14, 2019).
